asof: Settles Fri 30 Oct 2026 · written Sat 31 Oct
headline: Fed hawks pin the 2026–27 SR3 contracts while 2028–29 rally 2–4.5bp; U7 peak 4.52% still above the Fed's dots.
summary: The strip split on Friday: U6 to Z7 settled within 1bp of Thursday (Z6 unchanged at 4.145%, H7 and M7 up 1bp to 4.355% and 4.48%), while H8 to Z9 fell 2–4.5bp in implied rate, led by H9 down 4.5bp to 4.405%. On the week the rally is intact, with U7 9bp, Z7 10.5bp and H8 and M8 11bp lower since the 23 October settle. October ends with Z6 15.5bp, M7 32.4bp and Z7 38.2bp below the end-September (modelled) settles. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.52%, 58bp over the latest 3.94% SOFR fixing with 12.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9, roughly one hike more than the Fed's median and the consensus call of a December hike followed by a long hold.
drivers: Fed hawks out of blackout hold the front

Dallas Fed's Logan said at least two more 25bp hikes are needed, St. Louis Fed's Musalem said more firming is needed soon, and Richmond's Barkin called the direction clear but the pace gradual. That stopped the 2027 rally: Z6 was unchanged, H7 and M7 rose 1bp in rate and Z6/M7 widened 1bp to +33.5bp.
Tech sell-off sends money into the back of the strip

Worry that AI spending will not pay off knocked MSCI's world index down more than 1%, and the 10-year yield fell 4.4bp to 4.945% (2-year −5.4bp to 4.602%), heading for its biggest monthly fall since late 2023. In SR3 the bid went to 2028–29: H8 to Z9 fell 2–4.5bp, so U7/Z8 moved 4.5bp more inverted to −10bp.

The Q3 employment cost index rose 0.8%, as expected, with wages up 0.7% q/q and 3.1% y/y, the slowest annual pace since early 2021. Chicago PMI slipped to 55.3 against 56.0 expected, but its prices-paid index hit its highest since December 2021, so the data gave the market no reason to price out more of the December hike.
Oil up again, funding firm into month-end

Brent's expiring December contract rose $2.76 to $117.64 and WTI $1.98 to $104.12 after a tanker attack near Hormuz, both about 15% higher in October, which caps any rally in the whites. SOFR printed 3.94% for 29 October, above the 3.90% interest on reserves and 6bp over the 3.88% EFFR, and U6 held at 3.9225% through the month-end trade.
spreads: The whites were steady and the reds steepened. U6/Z6 held at +22.25bp (−9.9bp in October), Z6/H7 widened 1bp to +21bp (−10.6bp), H7/M7 was unchanged at +12.5bp (−6.3bp), M7/U7 narrowed 0.5bp to +4bp and U7/Z7 slipped 1bp to −2.5bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 was 0.5bp narrower at +35bp, 7bp narrower on the week and 22.7bp narrower than at end-September; Z6/M7 rose 1bp to +33.5bp but is 4.5bp narrower on the week and 16.9bp in October. Beyond the peak the curve inverted further as the 2028–29 contracts rallied: Z7/H8 −1.5bp to −3bp, Z7/Z8 −3.5bp to −7.5bp (about where it was a week ago) and U7/Z8 −4.5bp to −10bp, while Z8/Z9 held at −2.5bp; there is no October base for these before 20 October. Flies were steady: H7/M7/U7 +0.5bp to +8.5bp (−3.25bp in October) and M7/U7/Z7 +0.5bp to +6.5bp.
fed: Fed funds futures were last recorded at Thursday's close, with no Friday snapshot yet: 17.6bp for the 9 December meeting (a 70% chance of a hike), 24.5bp by January, 36.7bp by March, 51.6bp by June and a 55.5bp peak by December 2027 (implied EFFR 4.435%). That compares with 21.8bp, 48.1bp by March and a 75.5bp peak the day before, 21.2bp, 41.3bp and 62.5bp a week earlier, and 30.6bp, 63.4bp and 94bp at end-September, so October took out almost 40bp of tightening. SR3 now agrees with ZQ: the 4.435% ZQ peak plus SOFR's 6bp premium over EFFR is about 4.495%, level with Z7 and 2.5bp below U7, though Z6 at 4.145% sits about 4bp under the January ZQ level plus that premium, a slightly softer read of December. The strip prices 58bp to the peak, roughly two more hikes; the Fed's median projects one more this year and none in 2027, and ING says the consensus is a December hike reversed in late 2027, while Logan wants at least two.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 4.5bp in favour at +33.5bp: it widened 1bp on Friday as Fed hawks kept M7 from rallying, but is still 4.5bp narrower on the week and 16.9bp narrower in October. With 13.5bp to target and 6.5bp to the stop, reward is about 2.1 times risk. Kept: wages at 3.1% y/y and ZQ's 70% December odds argue for one hike and a hold, not the extra 2027 move M7 still carries.
ideas.risk: A strong October payrolls report (55,000 expected) or hot ISM prices could revive a second 2027 hike and push the spread back toward +40bp.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open at −7.5bp, 0.5bp short of the entry level after gaining 3.5bp on Friday, when Z8's implied rate fell 4bp against 0.5bp for Z7. Only 10bp of easing is priced from Z7 to Z9 and 12.5bp from the U7 peak; target −25bp is 17.5bp away against 9.5bp to the stop, about 1.8 times. Keep at about half the core size: it paid on a risk-off day when the core gave back 1bp.
ideas.risk: If 2027 hikes keep coming out the reds can flatten toward zero and push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through the settlement week

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 settled at 3.9225% implied, unchanged on the day and 1.25bp lower on the week, while the latest SOFR fixing of 3.94% sits above it and above the 3.90% interest on reserves. Monday's coupon settlement and Thursday's settlement of $277bn of 6-, 13- and 26-week bills could keep fixings firm, and only U6's final week sees the December decision; revisit after the 5 November prints.
ideas.risk: If the Fed restarts bill purchases or month-end pressure fades, SOFR could drop back to 3.88–3.90% and leave a couple of bp on the table.

watch: ISM manufacturing; Treasury Q4 borrowing estimate; coupon settlement
ISM is seen at 54.7 from 54.5; prices paid and bill supply guidance matter for the whites and SOFR fixings.
Control of Congress shapes the fiscal and term-premium outlook for the reds; openings are seen at 7.11m.
Coupon sizes and the bill share drive the reds and funding; services prices test the 2027 hikes.
A heavy settlement day for SOFR and U6; claims have run below 200,000.
55,000 expected after 29,000, unemployment 4.2%, hourly earnings 0.3%; the main test for Z6/M7.
Escalation risk after the midterms with Brent near $118 is the main threat to fading 2027 hikes.
